cost.q: How much does an installation cost?
cost.a: Cost is set by your annual electricity consumption, your roof and the equipment chosen. After the free survey we give you a technical analysis and a clear costing for your own needs.

payback.q: How many years until the investment pays back?
payback.a: Payback depends on consumption habits, electricity tariffs and system size. Our free feasibility study calculates the payback period for your own case.

warranty.q: What do the warranty and service cover?
warranty.a: The panels and equipment carry manufacturer warranties. Beyond that we stay with you through installation workmanship, commissioning and after-sales technical support.

incentives.a: Energy you generate beyond your own need can be exported to the grid and netted against your consumption under the applicable regulations. We guide you through the application and permit process.

roof.q: Is my roof suitable for a solar system?
roof.a: Orientation, pitch, shading and usable area are assessed to decide suitability. That analysis happens during the free survey.

outage.q: Does the system keep running during a power cut?
outage.a: A standard solar system stops generating during an outage, for safety. In systems designed together with storage, designated critical loads keep being fed.

duration.a: It varies with system size and project conditions, but on residential projects installation and commissioning are usually finished within a few days. Permit processes can run 16-20 weeks.

f1.q: Who runs the permits and licensing?
f1.a: We run every stage with our own team: the call-letter application, project approval, the connection agreement, acceptance and the system usage agreement.

f2.a: It depends on the scope. On rooftop projects, survey to commissioning typically runs 16-20 weeks; on ground-mount projects the permit calendar can stretch it.

f3.q: How much will a solar system cut my electricity bill?
f3.a: The saving depends on your consumption profile, the system size and the installation type. We assess your generation and consumption data and put together a projection for your site.

f4.q: Is my roof suitable for solar?
f4.a: Orientation, pitch, load-bearing structure and shading all go into a suitability analysis. The free survey looks at your roof's potential in detail.

f5.q: Does the system keep running during a power cut?
f5.a: A standard solar system shuts down when the grid goes, for safety. A hybrid system built together with energy storage keeps feeding designated loads.

f6.q: Can solar be added to an existing building?
f6.a: In most cases, yes. Existing roofs are assessed structurally and a solar plant fitted afterwards.

f7.q: How much maintenance does a solar system need?
f7.a: Very little, as a PV system has no moving parts. Periodic checks and panel cleaning keep it performing for years.

f8.q: Can storage or an EV charger be added to my existing system?
f8.a: In many cases an existing solar system can be integrated with storage and EV charging. Suitability is assessed during the survey.

f1.q: Can storage be added to my existing PV system?
f1.a: In most cases, yes. Depending on how the existing system is built, integration comes either through a hybrid inverter conversion or an add-on storage unit.

f2.q: How long do the batteries last?
f2.a: LFP batteries generally have a 6,000+ cycle life. Depending on how they are used, that means 10-15 years of service or more.

f3.q: Does the system keep running during a power cut?
f3.a: Storage systems with a backup function step in when the grid goes and keep feeding designated loads.

f4.q: How does storage affect my bill?
f4.a: By putting the energy you generate to better use, it can reduce how much you draw from the grid and optimise your energy costs.

f5.q: How is the capacity I need decided?
f5.a: Consumption habits, installed solar capacity and your energy goals are analysed to arrive at the right capacity.

what.title: What is a heat pump?
what.p1: A heat pump is a high-efficiency climate system that provides heating, cooling and domestic hot water by drawing on the natural heat held in air, water or the ground. Rather than generating energy it transfers what is already there, giving high performance from low consumption. It suits everything from homes to commercial buildings, and it is built to last.

how.title: How does it work?
how.p1: A heat pump uses the natural heat around it to warm the building in winter, and reverses its cycle in summer to cool. Most of the energy it needs comes from nature and the rest from electricity, so one system delivers efficiency, comfort and low running costs together.

air.title: Air-Source Heat Pump
air.desc: Uses the energy in outdoor air for heating, cooling and hot water. The most popular choice for homes and commercial buildings.

water.title: Water-Source Heat Pump
water.desc: Draws its energy from groundwater, lakes or similar sources. Offers stable, high-efficiency operation.

geo.title: Ground-Source Heat Pump
geo.desc: Taps the steady natural temperature the ground holds year round. High efficiency and a long service life.

pool.title: Pool Heat Pump
pool.desc: Built to heat swimming-pool water economically and efficiently. Holds the water at the ideal temperature and stretches the season.

adv.a2: Covers heating, cooling and hot water in one system.
adv.a6: Long-lived and dependable in daily use.
adv.a8: Supports the use of renewable energy.

f1.q: Does a heat pump work efficiently in winter?
f1.a: Yes. Modern air-source heat pumps are built to run at low outdoor temperatures. With the right capacity and a proper design, they heat efficiently all year round.

f2.a: In most cases, no. A heat pump can cover heating, cooling and domestic hot water on its own. Depending on the region, the climate and the building, the solution can be hybrid or fully electric.

f3.q: Does it use a lot of electricity?
f3.a: No. Because a heat pump transfers energy rather than generating it, it can yield more heat energy than the electricity it consumes, which makes it far more efficient than conventional electric heating.

f4.a: Homes, villas, apartment buildings, offices, hotels, hospitals, schools, commercial businesses, industrial facilities and pools.

f5.q: Can a heat pump produce hot water?
f5.a: Yes. Alongside heating and cooling it also covers domestic hot water, so one central system replaces several.

f6.q: What does a pool heat pump do?
f6.a: It heats pool water economically and under control, extending the swimming season at lower running costs than conventional methods.

f7.q: Is it an environmentally sound choice?
f7.a: Yes. By cutting fossil-fuel use it helps bring carbon emissions down, and paired with renewable generation the benefit grows.

f8.q: What is the advantage of pairing it with PV?
f8.a: The electricity the heat pump needs can be supplied by your own solar generation. That integration lowers energy costs while strengthening independence and the long-term return on the investment.

f9.q: Does it work with underfloor heating?
f9.a: Yes. Heat pumps run at high efficiency with underfloor systems and keep the interior comfortable.

f10.q: Can it be used with existing radiators?
f10.a: With the right capacity and flow temperatures, yes. A project-specific survey and analysis is recommended.

f11.q: Can it be used without PV?
f11.a: Yes. A heat pump runs independently on grid electricity. PV integration simply adds savings and energy independence.

f2.a: It depends on the car's battery capacity, how full it already is, and the charger's power. AC charging suits daily use, while DC fast charging moves a lot of energy in a short window.

f3.q: Can chargers be installed in apartment buildings and residences?
f3.a: Yes. Solutions can be fitted in individual parking bays or in communal areas to match the existing infrastructure. Each project gets a technical assessment to settle the right model.

f4.q: Can it work together with a solar system?
f4.a: Yes. EV chargers integrate with existing or new solar plants, so the energy you generate goes into the car and your costs come down.

f5.q: How do I choose between AC and DC charging?
f5.a: AC suits homes, workplaces and anywhere cars stay parked for a while. DC fast charging is the choice for commercial sites with high vehicle turnover, fleet operations and public charging points.

f6.q: Can a business offer charging as a service?
f6.a: Yes. OCPP-compliant systems let user management, consumption tracking, remote monitoring and billing all be run centrally.

f7.q: How does an EV charger show up on my electricity bill?
f7.a: Consumption depends on the car, how often it is used and the annual mileage. In most cases an electric car costs less per kilometre in energy than a conventional one.

f8.q: Do you provide technical support after installation?
f8.a: Yes. After design and installation we commission the system and back it with technical support and maintenance so it runs safely and efficiently.

Areas.title: One system, four scales
Areas.intro: From homes to industry, farms to public buildings: the four lines we build are the same everywhere. What changes is which one leads, and at what scale.
Areas.listIntro: Every setting has its own consumption curve and its own constraint, and the system design follows from that.

konut.title: Homes & Private
konut.desc: In villas, detached houses and gated communities the rooftop array, battery, heat pump and charger come together as one system.
konut.p1: Energy made in the day is carried into the evening, so less is drawn from the grid.
konut.p2: During an outage the house switches to the battery on its own.
konut.p3: The car charges overnight on energy the roof made that day.

ticari.title: Commercial & Industrial
ticari.desc: In factories, warehouses, industrial estates and hotels, large roofs and land become high-capacity plants.
ticari.p1: Production runs by day, so the consumption curve lines up with the sun.
ticari.p2: The battery steps in at peak hours, cutting demand charges and peak penalties.
ticari.p3: Charging for fleets and customers runs off the same system.

tarim.title: Agricultural Sites
tarim.desc: For irrigation, greenhouses, cold storage and livestock operations, energy stops being the largest line on the books.
tarim.p1: Irrigation pumps run in the hours the sun is strongest.
tarim.p2: With agri-PV the same land both generates and farms.
tarim.p3: Cold storage keeps running off the battery through an outage.

kamu.title: Public & Institutional
kamu.desc: For municipalities, schools, hospitals and public buildings the energy budget becomes predictable and critical loads are protected.
kamu.p1: The institution gets a predictable energy cost spread across years.
kamu.p2: Critical loads keep drawing from the battery the moment supply fails.
kamu.p3: Public charging points run on the institution's own generation.

Cookies.title: Cookie Policy
Cookies.intro: This page explains which cookies minada.com.tr uses, what they do, and how you can change your decision.

s1.title: What is a cookie?
s1.p1: A cookie is a small text file your browser saves on your device when you visit a site. It lets the site remember you. Your browser's local storage does a similar job, and this policy covers both together.
s1.p2: Cookies are grouped by what they are for. Necessary ones exist so the site can work at all and need no consent. Nothing beyond those runs unless you allow it.

s2.title: The groups
s2.necessary: Necessary: things the site needs in order to function, such as your language preference and your cookie decision. Cannot be turned off.
s2.analytics: Analytics: measures in aggregate how much each page is read. Does not identify you as a person.
s2.marketing: Marketing: measures ad delivery and what visits from ads lead to.

s3.title: What is in use today
s3.intro: As of today this site keeps necessary records only. No third party analytics or advertising cookie is written, and no tracking request leaves the site. This table is updated whenever a new record is added.
s3.r1w: Remembers whether you want the site in Turkish or English.
s3.r2w: Stores the decision you make on this page so you are not asked again on every page. Kept in your browser's local storage and never sent to the server.

s4.title: Changing your decision
s4.p1: The "Cookie preferences" link at the foot of every page reopens the screen where you made your choice. You can withdraw consent there at any time.
s4.p2: You can also delete or block all cookies from your browser settings. If you block the necessary records, your language preference will not be remembered.

Privacy.title: Privacy and Data Protection Notice
Privacy.intro: This notice explains how your personal data is handled when you use this site, as required by article 10 of Turkish law no. 6698 on the protection of personal data (KVKK).

s1.title: Who is responsible
s1.p1: The data controller is MİNADA Enerji. You can reach us at the addresses below.

s2.title: What we process
s2.p1: The only place this site collects data is the quote and survey form. Filling it in sends us:
s2.i1: Your name, phone number, email address and city.
s2.i2: Optionally: the topic you are interested in, your property type, your monthly bill and whatever you write in the message field.
s2.p2: Beyond that, technical records of your visit are kept: the IP address, browser and request time that land in the server logs. These exist to keep the site up and to prevent abuse.
s2.p3: The site runs no analytics or advertising tracking at all. The cookie policy lists every record that is kept, one by one.

s3.title: Why we process it
s3.i1: To answer your enquiry, arrange a survey and prepare your quote.
s3.i2: To stay in touch with you before and during a contract.
s3.i3: To stop the form being filled in by automated software.
s3.i4: To meet obligations placed on us by law.

s4.title: The legal basis
s4.p1: We rely on the explicit consent you give when you submit the form. We also rely on necessity for entering into and performing a contract, compliance with our legal obligations, and our legitimate interests. You can withdraw your consent at any time.

s5.title: Who we share it with
s5.p1: We do not sell your data and we do not pass it to third parties for marketing. We use the following suppliers only to run the service:
s5.i1: Vercel: hosts the site and keeps the server logs.
s5.i2: Resend: delivers the contents of the form to us by email.
s5.i3: Cloudflare Turnstile: used for form spam protection, and sees your IP address while that protection is on.
s5.p2: These suppliers' servers are outside Türkiye, so your data is transferred abroad. With our own installation teams and partners we share only what the work requires.

s6.title: How long we keep it
s6.p1: We keep your enquiry for as long as our relationship lasts and for the limitation and retention periods the law sets. Once that ends, or once you ask us to, the record is deleted.

s7.title: Your rights
s7.p1: Article 11 of the KVKK gives you the right to:
s7.i1: Learn whether your personal data is being processed, and ask for information if it is.
s7.i2: Learn the purpose of the processing and whether it is being used accordingly.
s7.i3: Know the third parties the data is transferred to, in Türkiye or abroad.
s7.i4: Ask for correction if it has been processed incompletely or wrongly.
s7.i5: Ask for erasure or destruction where the conditions for it are met.
s7.i6: Ask that correction and erasure be notified to the third parties it was transferred to.
s7.i7: Object to a result reached against you purely by automated analysis.
s7.i8: Claim compensation if unlawful processing has caused you loss.

s8.title: How to apply
s8.p1: To exercise your rights, write to us with an application that lets us verify your identity. We will respond within thirty days at the latest.

s9.title: Cookies
s9.p1: Which cookies this site keeps, and how to change your decision, are set out on their own page.
